Can I bring a lawyer to my inquiry?.heading: 6.6. Inquiry Process
Can I bring a lawyer to my inquiry?.body:
1. Attendance of the inquiry participants is to be recorded.
2. No advocate can legally be permitted to assist a workman during the inquiry.
3. The charge is to be read over to the accused employee.
4. The concerned employee (Accused) is to be asked by the Inquiry Officer, whether he pleads guilty to the charge framed against him or not.
5. If the accused employee does not plead guilty then the Inquiry Officer will ask the Complainant/Management’s Representative, as the case may be to record his statement in support of the charge framed against the employee.
6. Upon completion of Complainant/Management Representative’s, statement(s) the employee concerned will be given opportunity to cross-examine the complainant/Management Representative.
7. This pattern is to be followed concerning the witnesses of the complainant/ Management Representative.
8. Complainant/Management‘s Representative and/or his witnesses must also produce documentary evidence, if any, in support of the charges while recording statement.
9. After completion of evidence from company’s side the employee concerned will be provided full opportunity to record his statement in defense and lead evidence, if he so desires.
10. Upon completion of the statement of the employee, the Complainant/Management’s Representative will be given an opportunity to cross-examine the employee and his defense witnesses, if any.
11. The Inquiry Officer, while recording inquiries, must obtain signatures of all participants, particularly, the signatures of accused employee on the relevant enquiry page before going to the next page of the inquiry.
12. The questions and answers must be recorded verbatim.
13. The Inquiry Officer should not appear to be acting as a prosecutor because the function of the Inquiry Officer is only to record evidence of the parties and forward his findings to the management whether he found the accused employee guilty to the charge or not.

Can I bring a lawyer to my inquiry?.heading: 6.5. Role of Inquiry Officer
Can I bring a lawyer to my inquiry?.body:
The inquiry officer will be responsible for inquiring and submit recommendations to the Corrective-Action Committee. In case where the subject employee or group of employees’ replies and also denies the allegations, then the subject employee or group of employees will be requested to appear before an inquiry officer and respond in detail again.
The inquiry officer will file his inquiry report at the end of the inquiry meeting along with all evidence and reports, which include audit report, employee statement, supervisor statement, incident report, supporting documents etc. The following process must be followed by the Inquiry Officer while conducting an Inquiry.

Can I bring a lawyer to my inquiry?.heading: 6.1.9. Suspension of Service
Can I bring a lawyer to my inquiry?.body:
Reference above, due to the severe nature of violation, the presence of the accused employee at work may cause difficulties to the investigation and conclusion of the case, the company has the right to temporarily suspend the work of that employee. The suspension period should not exceed more than four days at a time (however, the total period of such suspension shall not exceed maximum of 28 working days). Suspension days’ salary will be with half pay.
The Li ne Manager should consult with respective HRBP before an employee is suspended. HRBP to issue letter of suspension and Show Cause Letter to the accused employee.
6.1.10. Steps to be followed in case of Inquiry
The manager responsible of the respective department will submit the incident report along with evidence to Human Resource Department.
Retail Excellence Manager along with concerned Area /Line Manager will be the manager responsible for retail field (all levels) of respective region.
For Head Office staff issues concerned HOD will be the responsible manager.
6.1.10.1. After receiving the case detail from concerned department, Human Resource department will ensure that the following supporting documents and evidence is received.
Incident report
Supporting evidence (if any).
Audit report from audit department (if required).
The HR department will then begin the inquiry proceedings and issue a show cause notice to the concerned employee or group of employees.
The accused will have four days to respond to the show cause notice. In case the employee refuses to accept the allegations mentioned in the Show Cause Notice, an Inquiry will be conducted to further investigate the matter. The following letters will be issued in case of Inquiry Proceedings.
Intimation Letter to Employee (Holding of Inquiry & Appointment of Inquiry Officer by Management & Suspension)
Suspension Letter (If to be Issued Separately)
Appointment of Inquiry Officer
Notice of Inquiry, by Inquiry Officer
In case the employee doesn’t respond to the show cause notice then a second notice will be issued. Failure to reply to even second show cause, the subject employee or group of employees will be regarded as accepting the accusations filed against the employee or group of employees.
In case an employee accepts the allegations in response to and as mentioned in the show cause notice the Corrective-Action committee will conclude as per the framework of the policy.

Can I bring a lawyer to my inquiry?.heading: 6.7. Inquiry Report
Can I bring a lawyer to my inquiry?.body:
1. The Inquiry report must be separately recorded by the Inquiry Officer discussing the evidence which comes on record during the Inquiry proceedings and that how he reached the conclusion about the charge being proved or not against the concerned employee.
2. Any extraneous and irrelevant consideration of evidence by the Inquiry Officer will not be legal.
3. This report will be brought to the Corrective-Action committee and concerned department \section\region head by the inquiry officer where the Corrective-Action committee upon full hearing and examination of evidence will make their recommendation for Corrective-Action Action.
4. In case of (Theft, Shortage, Fire, Strike, Malfunctioning, Unauthorized movement of stock/cash/assets etc.) where allegations are proved and agreed by Corrective-Action committee. Area managers from retail & ASM from will initiate the FIR for their respective business areas as per the recommendation by the Corrective-Action committee. (only in case FIR has already not been launched before as mentioned in clause 7.6)
5. After the filing of FIR or any action which involves legal proceedings, HR representative will provide support to respective ASMs or related departments in follow up of cases with our legal consultants.

Can I take a new PF loan while my old on.heading: 4. Eligibility Criteria:
Can I take a new PF loan while my old on.body:
4.1. An employee becomes eligible to apply for a PF Loan upon completion of at least Nine (09) months of continuous service with the company.
4.2. Eligibility criteria shall apply uniformly to all employees as per Annexure A, based on length of service duly recommended by concerned Line Manager, subject to further review by HR Team and approval by the Head of HR.
4.3. Any outstanding PF Loan must be fully settled prior to the disbursement of a new PF Loan.
4.4. Employees must submit a duly completed PF Loan Application Form Annexure B or initiate the request through the ESS workflow, along with all required approvals, prior to processing.

Can I take a new PF loan while my old on.heading: 6. Loan Repayment Terms:
Can I take a new PF loan while my old on.body:
6.1. The PF Loan shall be fully recovered through equal monthly installments, deducted directly from the employee’s salary via payroll during the employee’s tenure.
6.2. The maximum repayment period shall be as per Annexure A (mentioned below).
6.3. In case of early settlement of the outstanding PF Loan, the employee may request HR to deduct the partial or full amount from salary or deposit it directly into the company’s designated bank account, with proper intimation. Upon confirmation from Finance & Accounts, HR shall process the necessary payroll adjustments accordingly.
6.4. In case of resignation, termination or retirement, the outstanding PF Loan shall be adjusted against the employee’s PF balance through Full & Final Settlement with the Company.

Can I take a new PF loan while my old on.heading: 11. Employee Separation:
Can I take a new PF loan while my old on.body:
Upon separation from the Company, any outstanding Provident Fund (PF) Loan balance shall be adjusted and recovered through the employee’s Full & Final Settlement payment.
If the outstanding PF Loan amount exceeds the available PF balance, the excess amount shall be recovered from any other dues payable to the employee. If dues are insufficient, the matter shall be escalated to Administration Department (Legal section) for appropriate legal recovery.

Can I take a new PF loan while my old on.heading: 5. PF Loan Entitlement:
Can I take a new PF loan while my old on.body:
5.1. An employee shall be eligible to apply for a PF Loan based on the Employee and Employer contributions, subject to the conditions and limits defined in Annexure A.
5.2. The maximum PF Loan amount shall not exceed the eligible PF balance, as defined in Annexure A, at the time of application.
5.3. PF Loans shall be interest-free, as the loan is extended against the employee and employer Provident Fund balance.

Can I take a new PF loan while my old on.heading: 10. Loan Processing & Disbursement Timeline:
Can I take a new PF loan while my old on.body:
10.1. PF Loan requests will be processed within five (05) to seven (07) working days after complete documentation.
10.2. In case of an incomplete PF Loan request, it shall be returned to the applicant for rectification or completion of requirements.
10.3. Disbursement shall be made via bank transfer along with the monthly payroll or earlier, if requested and approved.
